subject: Foray #1 — grilling & world barbecue
purpose: Prioritised ASR work order, re-sorted against the 40-beat spine (docs/curation/grilling-history-spine.md) on 2026-08-17. Priority 1 is the material that would move a CHAIN beat off empty, Act IV first. That ordering is the whole point: 19 of the 24 empty beats are in chains and 5 are in the fan, and a hole in a chain reads to a listener as a missing link while a hole in a fan reads as a change of subject. So a fan hole is cheap and a chain hole is not, and CPU should be spent accordingly. Rows that buy an already-strong beat, that buy no beat at all, or that are unusable under the English-only ruling carry `priority: null` and a `blocked_by` reason. They are kept, never pruned.
companions: docs/curation/catalogue-broadening.md — where the new sources came from, and which traditions stayed unsourceable
docs/curation/grilling-foray-passages.md — the 8 passages that already exist (8:21)
committed_here_because: docs/curation/ carries no source prose — only feed metadata we measured ourselves — and data-local/ is gitignored, so a manifest placed there would be invisible to every other checkout and to cloud runners. Same call as docs/curation/grilling-foray-passages.json.

method.ad_free_ratio: delivered bytes / feed-declared enclosure length, via a 2-byte ranged GET reading the true total from Content-Range (tools/transcribe/ad-inflation.mjs). HEAD lies on ad-inserting hosts and was not used. Threshold < 1.01.
method.true_duration: itunes:duration from the feed, cross-checked against declared_bytes*8/duration landing on a standard bitrate. Rows where the feed declares length=0 or length=1 cannot use the byte method and are labelled bitrate-implied.
method.duration_gaps: None. Every row below carries an itunes:duration read from its feed; there is no row whose true duration could not be obtained.

excluded_by_instruction: The BBQ Central Show — already being transcribed by the American-arc workstream. Note that data/transcript-availability.json records 1,858 episodes on that feed of which 12 carry a <podcast:transcript> tag, and only one is on plot: the Moss BBQ School episode already segmented.

The British Food History Podcast — already being transcribed. Separately, and more decisively: of the 13 bfh-* segments in the pool, exactly one survived stage 2's beat-level gate and only as an alternate. This is the drift the founder named. Nothing here is queued for this Foray.

Stuff You Should Know — A Lip-Smacking Look at Barbecue. Ships a timed transcript and needs no ASR, and is EXCLUDED on the register rather than on availability: two hosts working from an article, no guest, no sourced expertise, and it contains the line that barbecue 'kind of transcends race and class' twenty seconds after its Jim Crow passage — which is the harmony version beat 23 exists to reject. Admitting a source the narrative refutes is the failure #226 was opened to fix. This returns beats 7, 19, 24 and 30 to empty and to narration.

read_this_before_spending_cpu.language_gate: SETTLED, not open. docs/DECISIONS.md records the English-only ruling (Wyatt, 2026-08-16) with the narrator ruling: non-English tape is not shipped, and the narrator describes those traditions in English instead. Ten of the 24 rows here are non-English and are therefore unqueued with `blocked_by: english-only-ruling` — 3.43 h of audio that no longer has a claim on CPU. An earlier draft of the coverage report and catalogue-broadening.md §3 both still frame this as unresolved; they are wrong and reconciling them would stop the next agent re-deciding it.
read_this_before_spending_cpu.unfillable_slots: braai (beat 13) and Filipino lechon have no source at any budget after a 4.71M-feed search. The mangal/kebab root of beat 9 has one candidate and it fails the CONTENT gate, which neither ad measurement nor ASR fixes. Beat 8 (the steppe) has no source found and none proven absent. Tandoor (beat 10) is NO LONGER in this list: ADR-0008 removed the ad gate the earlier verdict rested on. See catalogue-broadening.md §4, whose §0 summary still calls tandoor unsourceable and is stale.
read_this_before_spending_cpu.spend_this_first: Reading beats transcribing. Two of the four identified Act IV sources may already ship transcripts. Reading SYSK's is what produced four verdict changes in stage 2 for one fetch — and then the founder ruled the register out, which is itself the argument for reading before spending: the cheap check is what tells you whether the expensive one is worth it.

totals.cost_note: The rate that matters is the observed one. tools/transcribe measured 1.33x for base.en and the live whisper queue is running at 0.475x because of contention, so an hour of audio is about 2.1 CPU-hours in practice, not 1.1. The point of the re-sort is that it makes the queue much shorter as well as better ordered: ten non-English rows and four no-beat rows leave the queue entirely, and priority 1 is now three episodes rather than eight.
totals.what_priority_1_costs_and_buys: Two measured rows here total 6,772 s (1.88 h, about 4.0 CPU-hours observed), and the third (Gastropod, ~49 min) is in identified_not_yet_measured pending a probe. For that, up to seven chain beats move off empty — 18, 20, 21, 22, 38 and 31, plus beat 2 — against the OLD priority 1, which was 3.43 h of audio and moved none.

spine_realignment.why_the_old_order_was_wrong: The old order was sorted by value against the six arc slots in data/forays.json, and the spine's 40 beats are a different instrument. Measured against the beats, NONE of the eight priority-1 rows moved a chain beat off empty: three bought beats that are already strong (1, 14, 15), one bought a beat that does not exist in the spine at all (Santa Maria), three are unusable under the English-only ruling, and the eighth (the Korean episode) does not advance beat 12 on its stated subject. Meanwhile the single most valuable episode in the manifest sat at priority 3.
spine_realignment.what_priority_1_is_now: Three rows. The Grill Coach/Adrian Miller episode (beats 18, 20, 21, 22, 38), the Moreish/Goucher episode (beat 20, plus 2 and 15), and Gastropod's 'The Birth of Cool' (beat 31, Act V's chain hinge), which was previously filed under excluded_by_instruction on a workstream note rather than a rejection.
spine_realignment.what_it_buys: Up to seven chain beats, including beat 21 — which the spine says decides whether the Foray is worth shipping — and beats 20, 22 and 38, which with 21 are the 12 % of runtime the spine calls the honest weight of the authorship argument. Act IV today has no strong tape anywhere in it across fifteen beats and 36.5 % of the spine's runtime, and three of its four authorship beats are empty. Nothing else in this manifest touches that.
spine_realignment.cheaper_than_asr_and_therefore_first: Two of the four identified Act IV sources may already ship transcripts, and reading one is what produced four verdict changes in the stage 2 report for the cost of a single fetch. Read Proof (America's Test Kitchen) and check A Taste of the Past for a transcript BEFORE buying any ASR. See identified_not_yet_measured below.
spine_realignment.what_no_amount_of_asr_buys: Beats 11 (yakitori), 12 (Korea) and 17 (barbacoa as living practice) have sources that are not in English, so they are permanent narration beats under the English-only ruling. Beat 13 (braai) and beat 9's Ottoman/mangal root have no source that passes the content gate at any budget. Beat 8 (the steppe) has no source found and none proven absent. Of the five empty fan beats only beat 10 (tandoor) could be closed by measuring and transcribing, and it is a fan hole, so it is cheap.

identified_not_yet_measured._comment: Act IV and Act V sources named in stage 2's coverage report and in docs/adr/0008-ad-tolerance-and-timestamp-precision.md that have NO measured row in `episodes` yet. Deliberately recorded without feed metadata: this pass did not fetch their feeds, and inventing a guid or an enclosure URL is how the wrong episode gets registered. Measure, then promote to a real row.

rows.episode_title: The Birth of Cool: How Refrigeration Changed Everything
rows.ad_status: PADDABLE. The one show in this repo probed twice by decode-and-compare (+66.1 s and +32.7 s), so about a 100 s pad against the 120 s ceiling. The `1.080 — injected` figure in grilling-foray-sourcing.md §4 is bitrate-implied AND against a different episode, and applying it here is the axis error ADR-0008 warns about; it overstated the real load by 3–6x.
rows.buys: Beat 31, the hinge of Act V and the mechanism that ends the necessity era Act I establishes. Beat 2 argues smoke is infrastructure and Act V assumes it stopped being so, with nothing narrating the transition, so the Foray's central irony is currently asserted at both ends and explained at neither. Publishes no timed transcript (0 of 293 episodes), so it needs ASR. Previously sat in excluded_by_instruction as 'already being transcribed', which is a workstream note, not a rejection.
rows.outstanding_caveat: Both Gastropod probes were the same client on the same day. Sample a different requester's copy before relying on the pad.
